notes.content:
[h2]NEW CHAMPIONS[/h2][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Mr. Knight (Summoners Choice Winner) [/h3][p]There is a time for a clenched fist and time for a helping hand. When Moon Knight wants to add nuance to his crime-fighting he takes on the persona of Mr. Knight. This gentleman detective can talk his way out of trouble, but is no stranger to rolling up his sleeves for more intensive interrogations.

[/p][h3]Silver Samurai[/h3][p]Kenuichio Harada is the mutant son of former Japanese crimelord Shingen Yashida, the head of the influential Clan Yashida in Japan. Harada has mastered the disciplines of the Samurai, with his mutant powers granting him the ability to generate energy from within himself, and transfer said energy through inanimate objects. He uses this gift to empower his sacred Katana, allowing it to cut through nearly anything. Now, like his father, he seeks to run his own criminal underworld.

[/p][p][/p][h2]CHAMPION UPDATES[/h2][p]Rhino
The same Rhino, with a bunch of new power. Dash around the stage to build furies and deal a ton of Damage.
The first Champion with the new "Breach" type. He can now go even more consistently unblockable.
Dash a lot, it's really what he wants to do. Take control of the stage and blast.

[/p][h2]NEW QUESTS AND EVENTS[/h2][p]
[/p][h3]Act 9 Chapter 3 - Vengeance[/h3][p]Lotan, the cursed hammer of Jane Foster, has fallen silent but the threats to The Contest are far from over. Those who appeared as friends reveal their villainous intent. Those who are meant to protect are finding their shields a bit too heavy to carry. Nobody trusts anybody now, and they’re all very tired. But not all hope is lost, there are still those who are willing to fight for the sake of The Battlerealm. The only question is, will they trust The Summoner to fight alongside them as they face down their biggest challenge to date?

[/p][h3]Event Quest  - In This Corner[/h3][p]Try out this new Event Quest featuring ADAPTIVE DIFFICULTY which will tune the battle to best challenge and reward your roster! If you’re feeling up to the challenge and want the best possible rewards, toggle on Elder Difficulty which will increase difficulty and allow you to climb further in the milestone reward track! 

Maestro seeks to ensure The Battlerealm is defended, but his methods may not be for everyone. The often contested territory of New Manhattan seeks a protector, and The Summoner is called in to help with a fight tournament. Leading their own teams of fighters are SILVER SAMURAI and Summoner’s Choice Champion MR. KNIGHT! Will this fight reveal New Manhattan’s latest hero, or will it break out as a city-wide rumble?

[/p][h3]Side-Quest - Boss Rush: Big Blue (Starting September 10)[/h3][p]The Blue Area of the Moon has served as a space of relative peace within the constant conflict of the Battlerealm. However, rumors of an abandoned Watcher’s citadel have led multiple miscreants to invade the city in search of advanced alien technology. The Fantastic Four are quick to react and send the Summoner out to impede this archeological plundering.

Each week you’ll be able to earn up to 4x chances to face down 5x challenging Bosses of a single Class.

[/p][h3]Fantastic Fun Fall Fair Event (Starting September 17)[/h3][p]The Fair is coming to the Battlerealm! Take on Fantastic Four-themed Solo Objectives and Arenas to win Prize Vouchers which can be exchanged for prize bundles that include Crystals, Crystal shards, Gold and more!

[/p][h3]Mini Side-Quest - Food For Thought  (Starting September 24)[/h3][p]Mister Fantastic wants to ensure that you get one last chance to research strange and exciting new scientific discoveries. This Quest may seem simple, but participation is recommended as we head into a new Saga of adventures and discoveries.

[/p][h2]BUG FIXES AND IMPROVEMENTS:[/h2][p]
Daily Quest Updates - Progression tuned improvements are coming to Daily Quests along with new Supply Runs and Supply Strikes! Play daily to maximize your rewards and resources! Check your in-game mail for more information.

All this and more! Check out the complete list of exciting updates on [url="https://playcontestofchampions.com/"]playcontestofchampions.com[/url][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary: Questing and Alliance Updates
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Summoners![/p][p]
As part of our continuing goal of bringing new and innovative experiences to The Contest, we aim to make The Battlerealm more dynamic, rewarding, and fun for Summoners of all levels. [/p][p]Today, we dive into a trio of updates coming to Marvel Contest of Champions in September 2025, and we can’t wait for you to jump into the new Adaptive Difficulty Event Quest, the revamped Alliance Weekly Super Event, and explore the Daily Quest Rework. These changes are designed to streamline gameplay, reward teamwork, and offer challenges tailored to your progression. Let’s break it all down.[/p][p][/p][h1]Adaptive Difficulty Event Quest[/h1][p]We’re revitalizing the monthly Event Quest with the introduction of Adaptive Difficulty. 
Starting in September, we’re moving away from the traditional six difficulty tiers (Contender, Proven, Conquerer, Cavalier, Uncollected, and Thronebreaker) to a single, dynamic difficulty that scales to your roster and progression level.[/p][p][/p][h2]Here’s how it works -[/h2][p]Personalized Scaling: The Adaptive Difficulty Event Quest adjusts its challenge based on your account’s progression (Cavalier, Thronebreaker, Valiant, etc) and Top 30 Prestige. 
Our aim is to ensure the quest feels appropriately challenging, whether you’re a new Summoner or a seasoned veteran. We believe that by consolidating the six difficulties into one, we’ll be providing a streamlined Event Quest experience that will appropriately scale as you progress your account through the Battlerealm. Rewards will also scale with the difficulty, ensuring higher-progression players earn rewards commensurate with their roster strength, while newer players still get meaningful progression items without feeling the need to do multiple difficulties.
[/p][p]This change allows us to craft richer, more focused Event Quests that deliver a cohesive narrative and gameplay experience tailored to YOU. We’ve heard your feedback over the years that our monthly content feels stale, and Adaptive Difficulty is our solution for more engaging and always up to date Event Quests.
[/p][p]Speaking of that, we also heard your feedback on our Valiant Event Quest Test Runs.
If you’re PARAGON & ABOVE, you’ll be able to toggle on the new ELDER Difficulty, unlocking a more challenging version of the Event Quest that closely mirrors the structure of the first iteration of our Valiant EQ test. Elder Difficulty is meant to make our monthly content feel impactful even to our most engaged players. The first iteration will likely look familiar to you, and we may experiment with other formats in the future.
[/p][h2]Why the Change?[/h2][p]With Adaptive Difficulty, we’re able to allocate more resources to creating unique nodes, memorable boss fights, and exciting story beats. Instead of splitting our design efforts across six static difficulties, we’re pouring our energy into one quest that adapts to your skill and roster.  Get ready to face the latest threats of the Battlerealm in a way that feels personal and rewarding.
[/p][h2]Prestige Going Forward[/h2][p]On the topic of Top 30 Prestige, starting in October, Alliance Quest and Alliance Raids will transition to a Top 30 Prestige System, moving away from the current Top 5 Champion and Relic Prestige model. Going forward, your Top 30 Champions and Top 30 Relics will combine to account for your Top 30 Prestige. [/p][p]This change aims to streamline Prestige across the Battlerealm, offering a broader and more inclusive approach to roster strength in these game modes. Alongside this update, we're wanting to make managing prestige a lot easier. There will be a top 30 prestige view, and you will also be able to sort your roster by prestige.[/p][p]We’ll dive deeper into the details of this shift and what it means for your Alliance in its own dedicated post coming soon![/p][p]  [/p][h1]Alliance Weekly Super Event[/h1][p]The Alliance Weekly Super Event is here to replace the Summoner Advancement and Engagement events, which kicked off on August 11 and will run weekly going forward.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Key Features:[/h2][p]Similar to the Daily Super Event, the Alliance Weekly Super Event offers rewards earned through collective alliance activities like Alliance Quest, Alliance War, Battlegrounds, and Incursions. The higher your alliance’s milestone, the better the rewards, including T7B shards, Glory, and more.
[/p][p]The Alliance Weekly Super Event will be utilizing Peak Milestone rewards, meaning rewards are distributed based on the highest milestone your alliance achieves by the end of the week.[/p][p]While units have been shifted to the upcoming Daily Quest Rework (more on that below), the Alliance Weekly Super Event includes valuable resources to fuel your journey in the Battlerealm.[/p][p][/p][p]We’ve seen some community concerns about the absence of certain rewards like energy refills, revives, and boosts in the initial Alliance Weekly Super Event rollout. We definitely understand those concerns in particular because the Daily Quest Rework was initially slated to launch alongside this update where you’d have seen the majority of these rewards allocated throughout. That being said, we’re actively listening to your feedback and working to ensure this event feels as rewarding as intended. 
[/p][h1][b]Daily Quest Rework:[/b][/h1][p]Starting in September, the Daily Quest Rework will transform your daily gameplay into a more rewarding experience. We’re replacing the current class-based Catalyst quests with a new structure focused on variety and accessibility. These are meant to be auto-playable content, and are a great way to kick off your Daily Super Event earnings.[/p][p][/p][h2]What’s Changing?[/h2][p]Daily Quests will now have two always active quests, one geared toward resources (Gold, ISO-8, etc.) and the other on Catalysts of all tiers, including lower-level ones for newer (or nostalgic) players.  We’ll also be introducing our Supply Run Daily Quests. These run Monday through Saturday, with each day offering different materials. Units previously earned through Alliance Events have been moved to the Daily Quests so you’ll need to use energy to access these rewards, but we’ve balanced the costs to keep them fair. Completing a Supply Run will earn you a Supply Intel that you can use to enter the Super Version of this Supply Run Quest on Sundays. It will take 4 Supply Intels to enter, and the Sunday Run is extra juicy - so make sure you’re playing these![/p][p][/p][p]This rework aims to make Daily Quests a consistent source of progression resources while giving you more control over what you prioritize each day. Whether you’re hunting for 7 Star Sig Stones or stocking up on Gold, there’s something for every Summoner. With the addition of Supply Run Daily Quests and the Super Run on Sundays, every quest offers greater value than ever before, ensuring your time in the Battlerealm yields richer rewards to accelerate your roster’s growth.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Addressing Energy Refills in the Alliance Weekly Super Event:[/h2][p]We want to be transparent about a change to the Alliance Weekly Super Event that’s tied to the introduction of Adaptive Difficulty in Event Quests. Previously, the Alliance Events included energy refills to support tackling multiple Event Quest difficulties. With the shift to a single Adaptive Difficulty Event Quest, the total cost of energy across multiple tiers has been significantly reduced. As a result, we’ve scaled back the number of energy refills available in the Alliance Weekly Super Event to align with this streamlined experience.[/p][p][/p][p]As we move beyond 10 years of The Contest, it is important that we iterate, innovate, adapt and grow. That sometimes means the things we update and revamp may not always be on a 1:1 ratio or we allocate them in different areas as you’ll see with the Daily Quest Rework.
[/p][p]With that, we do understand energy is a hot topic - many of you have voiced concerns about energy costs and caps, and we hear you loud and clear. We hope that you’ll find value in this change and know that we’ll continue exploring ways to optimize energy usage across the game.  As always, we’ll continue to monitor your feedback to ensure the Alliance Weekly Super Event and Daily Quests feel rewarding and sustainable. And of course, if you have thoughts on how we can improve, please share them on the forums or other Community spaces.
[/p][h1][b]Looking Ahead[/b][/h1][p]These updates mark a bold step forward for Marvel Contest of Champions. We aim to keep the Battlerealm fresh with these changes, and we’re excited to see how you engage with the Adaptive Difficulty Event Quest, Alliance Weekly Super Event, and Daily Quest Rework. We’re committed to iterating on these systems based on your feedback, so keep those comments coming in the usual spaces.[/p][p]
[/p][p]Thank you for your passion and dedication to The Contest.[/p]

notes.title: 52.0.0 is now live!
notes.content:
[h2]NEW CHAMPIONS[/h2][p]
[/p][h3]Solvarch[/h3][p]The result of this nightmarish design, an Eidol whose thirst for destruction is matched only by his hunger for power. With the ability to freeze their opponent with a mere touch, they hunger to absorb all the power in The Battlerealm, before releasing this overwhelming power on any who would dare stand in their way.

[/p][h3]Cassandra Nova[/h3][p]A manifestation of negative potential that is a dark reflection of all the psionic power and potential of Charles Xavier. This sister was thought to be destroyed but somehow she rebuilt herself cell by cell for decades. Now, wielding power and hate in equal measure, she seeks to destroy all that her brother has built.


[/p][h2]CHAMPION UPDATES[/h2][p]M.O.D.O.K. and Yondu have been fully reworked, and Patriot has been rebalanced.
Check out our Blog for more specifics on these exciting updates.

[/p][h2]NEW QUESTS AND EVENTS[/h2][p]
[/p][h3]Event Quest - Broken Dreams[/h3][p]Solvarch, Wolf of the Stars, is a formidable foe capable of draining energy at the atomic level from those who dare oppose them. This danger is made all the worse by a second villainous arrival: Cassandra Nova. This mentally manipulative monster seeks to torture The Summoner while allowing Eidol threats to grow. Will The Contest be able to recover from this double dose of danger?

[/p][h3]The Crucible[/h3][p]Available starting August 13. Old foes have returned and are more dangerous than before. Enter the all new Crucible Quest Chapter: Act 8 - The Rebirth and fight your way through a gauntlet of Act 8 bosses. Be wary and stay vigilant, as your arsenal of Champions will need to be vast to overcome this plethora of unrelenting challenges. A fruitful reward will be at the ready for any Summoner courageous enough to battle their way through and conquer these combatants once and for all. This Quest will be available permanently, even after the Rebirth Event has passed!

notes.title: Rebirth Champion Updates
notes.content: [h2]Overview[/h2][p]The August Rebirth Event features a pool of Champions released at the 7-Star rarity for the first time! That pool is:[/p][list][*][p]Viv Vision[/p][/*][*][p]Cull Obsidian[/p][/*][*][p]Doctor Voodoo[/p][/*][*][p]Anti-Venom[/p][/*][*][p]Night Thrasher[/p][/*][*][p]Sabretooth[/p][/*][/list][p]Any time we prepare for the release of Champions at a new rarity, we seek to ensure they can land as well as possible to progress the game and provide Summoners with a fun experience. This involves taking into account how they can be obtained, how they fit into the meta-game of The Contest, and their general power level, just to name a few considerations. Sometimes, these factors lead us to ask questions like “Should we update this Champion,” or “If we wanted to, would we even have time amidst everything else we’re doing?” The small updates to Abomination (Immortal) in the Heart of Fire event is a recent example of this.[/p][p][/p][p]In the case of the Rebirth pool, we identified that all the Champions [i]could[/i] be released as-is, but that we would love to update some of them. In this case, our Champion and Balance teams were just able to squeeze in updates to everyone we felt could benefit from modernization–all of them with the exception of Viv Vision, who only received some small cleanup and bug fixes because we already expect her to be quite a powerful addition to the 7-Star roster. All six champions benefited from a thorough bug pass, though, and will perform a bit more reliably because of that.[/p][p][/p][h2]Context[/h2][p]Before dropping the full change log below, we want to be really clear about expectations for future additions of Champions to the 7-Star or any new-to-them rarity: our general goal is to release fun, relevant Champions. As time allows, for any pool of Champions released at a new tier, we may want to perform a small update of anyone we feel falls too short of a modern Champion, with consideration of the acquisition method in mind.[/p][p][/p][p]What exactly does “as time allows” mean? What is the definition of a healthy, interesting, usable, modern Champion? How does the acquisition method matter? These are nuanced and situational enough that we want to consider these on a case-by-case basis rather than trying to establish some rigid guidelines. The above philosophy will be our guiding light, and this experience will inform future similar cycles just as Abomination (Immortal) in Heart of Fire informed this one.[/p][p][/p][p]With that said, the changes to this pool of Champions ended up being a bit bigger than initially expected–in no small part due to the fact that some of them are relatively old kits, but also because they’re so beloved by some of the designers. We are thrilled to bring you these updates and hope you enjoy them as much as we enjoyed making them.[/p][p][/p][h2]Change Log[/h2][h3]Cull Obsidian[/h3][list][*][p]Added: start with 3 Persistent Charges in Battlegrounds and Alliance War fights[/p][/*][*][p]Removed Mission 3’s 95% Health threshold requirement[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Thanos’ Favor Buff on-hit pause duration from 1 to 2.5 seconds[/p][/*][*][p]Swapped Thanos’ Favor Buff effects for 3 and 5 stacks. 3 Thanos’ Favor Buffs now provides True Accuracy and 5 grants Critical Damage Rating[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Special Attack 2 Armor Break pause chance from 80% to 100%[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Special Attack 2 Armor Break pause duration from 2 to 5 seconds[/p][/*][/list][h3]Doctor Voodoo[/h3][list][*][p]Added: While above 1 Bar of Power, Heavy Attack consumes 0.5 Bars to apply a Loa Buff[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked Special Attack 2 [/p][list][*][p]Last hit has 3 independent 65% chances to Nullify a Loa and either gain a Buff or inflict a Debuff, based on combo[/p][list][*][p]Even: Voodoo’s attacks gain a 50% chance to Steal 2.5% of his Opponent’s Max Power, gaining 10% of the Power Stolen. Max stacks: 3.[/p][/*][*][p]Odd: Voodoo inflicts a 2% Power Dissolve Debuff for 10 seconds. Max stacks: 3.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]Anti-Venom[/h3][list][*][p]Added: Personal Passives are paused during Specials and for 5 seconds on Striker activation.[/p][/*][*][p]Changed Genetic Memory Debuff application trigger from every 10 hits in either Champion’s Combo Meter to every 10 times either Champion is struck[/p][/*][*][p]Changed Klyntar Debuff against Mystic Champions 100% Ability Accuracy Reduction trigger from 30 Combo Meter to while 4 or more of Anti-Venom’s personal Debuffs are active[/p][/*][*][p]Changed Special Attack 2 Genetic Memory Debuff consumption from all debuffs to all but the 2 most recent. Furies still gained based on total Genetic Memory Debuff count.[/p][list][*][p]Updated Lady Deathstrike Synergy to preserve the three most recent[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Removed Signature Ability Debuff potency scaling based on combo, and replaced with:[/p][list][*][p]Every time Anti-Venom inflicts a personal Debuff, he inflicts an indefinite 2.5% Exacerbate Passive. Max Stacks: 10.[/p][list][*][p]Exacerbate increases the Potency of new non-damaging Debuffs applied to the affected Champion by the listed amount.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Each personal Exacerbate Passive increases the potency of Anti-Venom’s personal Debuffs by an additional 2.5%.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]Night Thrasher[/h3][list][*][p]Added: Knocking down the opponent Purifies 1 Debuff on Night Thrasher[/p][/*][*][p]Added: Gadget Debuffs paused during all Special Attacks[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Gadget Debuff duration from 12 to 15 seconds[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Critical Damage Rating provided by each unique Debuff [/p][/*][*][p]Increased Special Attack 2’s Precision potency [/p][/*][*][p]Increased Special Attack 2’s Precision duration from 10 to 18 seconds[/p][/*][*][p]Removed scaling from Signature Ability Taunt application chance. Now always 35% chance per Gadget Debuff[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced potency of incoming Night Hawks synergy with Darkhawk to compensate for increased base kit damage output[/p][/*][/list][h3]Sabretooth[/h3][list][*][p]Added: Stun Debuffs on the Opponent cannot have their duration reduced[/p][/*][*][p]Clarified/Updated: the time required to convert a Fury Buff to a Passive has been shortened from 1.5 seconds to 1.4, but Sabretooth is incorrectly stating this delay is currently only 1 second, so it will read like an extension[/p][/*][*][p]Added: start with 5 Passive Furies (Combo-based potency) in Battlegrounds fights[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Combo-based Fury duration from 5 to 6 seconds[/p][/*][*][p]Added: Once Sabretooth has converted his maximum possible Furies per fight, Combo-based Furies gain 200% duration and 50% potency. [/p][/*][*][p]Increased Special Attack Bleed chance from 60% to 80%[/p][/*][*][p]Expanded Special Attack 1 Fury conversion trigger from first hit to first [i]and[/i] last hit[/p][/*][*][p]Added: Special Attack 2 also triggers a Regeneration effect for 10% of missing Health over 15 seconds[/p][/*][*][p]Expanded Signature Ability Regeneration trigger from when struck to when struck or when blocking a Critical Hit[/p][/*][/list][h3]Viv Vision[/h3][list][*][p]Solar Energy charges are no longer subject to Ability Accuracy[/p][/*][*][p]The Special 3 Fury is no longer subject to Ability Accuracy[/p][/*][*][p]Bug fix: Her Heavy Attack was only ever dealing extra damage for one Invalidate and now correctly scales to 3[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: BALANCE UPDATE: Arnim Zola and Falcon (Joaquin Torres)
notes.content:
[p]Hey all,
Balance Team here again with an update on the latest round of Champions up for review, Falcon (Joaquin Torres) and Arnim Zola! 
[/p][h1]Falcon (Joaquin Torres)[/h1][p] The Battlerealm’s newest Falcon in Joaquin Torres was designed to be a well-rounded Attacker, using a wide range of Debuffs to mitigate incoming Damage, counter his Opponent’s threats and enhance his damage output. While his kit features 2 distinct modes to choose from, Joaquin Torres thrives once he reaches Peak Performance, allowing him to benefit from both his Offensive and Defensive themed modes at the same time. Equipped with a few abilities targeted at annoying Mystic opponents (Slow, Debilitate, replacing the Precision Buff from Dexterity with a Trauma Pause), we’re happy to see his matchup spread reflect his targets, albeit with varying performance depending on the game mode. While Falcon’s performance is in a good spot in Quests with longer encounters and a wide range of opponents, we’re seeing Falcon struggle to get his loop going in encounters with shorter runway and higher pressure (e.g. Battlegrounds), and will be looking to make changes to address this. Changes incoming for Joaquin! 
[/p][h1]Arnim Zola[/h1][p] Arnim Zola entered the contest armed with a new spin on Tech Power Control with his combo of Special Lock and Combat Power Reduction, while also leveraging damage mitigation and loop disruption as his core Defensive identity. In PvP modes, Arnim Zola has landed and continued to make an impact as a powerful stall threat, with one of the highest average Defending fight times in Battlegrounds across recent seasons. Since release, we’ve seen summoners adapt to Arnim Zola’s unique defensive kit with a variety of strategies, and are happy with his impact on the meta. As an Attacker, the burst of Direct Damage granted by his Signature Ability has proven to be an important piece to his Damage reach, and is overall in a healthy range for a kit that heavily leans on Damage Mitigation and Power Control. Overall we’re happy with how Zola has landed and will not be making any changes to his kit! 
[/p][h1]What’s Next[/h1][p] [b]Falcon (Joaquin Torres)[/b] will be a part of [b]Batch Update #2[/b] - slated for our [b]54.1 (January)[/b] build! 

So far, the 2 confirmed Champions in Batch #2 are: [/p][list][*][p]Vision (Deathless)[/p][/*][*][p]Falcon (Joaquin Torres)[/p][/*][*][p]Champion TBD[/p][/*][/list][p] You can expect communication on JEAN GREY & BASTION toward the middle of AUGUST![/p]

notes.content: [h2]NEW CHAMPIONS[/h2][p][/p][h3]High Evolutionary:[/h3][p]Herbert Wyndham began experimenting with genetic manipulation in an attempt to “evolve” rats. He was later approached by a disguised Inhuman who would hand him the blueprints to unlock genetic code. This advanced his experiments to evolving animals into humanoids he called “New Men”. notes.title: Dev Diary: STATCAST RELICS
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Summoners,
Now we know you’ve been hearing about these Statcast Relics for some time and are probably wondering about the deep deets,  so we put together a bit of a behind-the-scenes info dive to get you ready for the upcoming Statcast Relics! With that, let’s start by answering a few questions.[/p][p]
[b]What happened with Battlecasts?[/b][/p][p]When we were making Battlecasts, there were a few different goals we were trying to achieve…[/p][list][*][p][b]Collectible[/b] - These should be desirable objects that players are excited to get[/p][/*][*][p][b]Scalable[/b] - Lots of design levers, easy to expand on[/p][/*][*][p][b]Theorycrafting[/b] - Players have lots of options to consider [/p][/*][*][p][b]Meaningful Choices[/b] - Decisions have real impacts 
[/p][/*][/list][p]In practice, what we found was…[/p][list][*][p][b]Too Complex (for players)[/b] - The data showed that many players weren’t making Rune selections at all. As a result, many players had an underwhelming first impression of Battlecasts, since the abilities they were designed to grant weren’t being selected by the player leading to those abilities not being enabled. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Too Flexible (for development)[/b] - Adding or modifying RPG abilities for an entire class is very challenging to balance. Whenever we introduced a new Battlecast, we had to make sure it didn’t break one of the ~40 Champions it could bind to, and whenever we create a new Champion, we have to make sure they aren’t broken with any of the existing Battlecasts. In many ways, building Battlecasts actually required more playtesting than did a new Champion, and our design team simply couldn’t sustainably support them.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Ultimately, this led us to a point where we could reasonably create about 3 Battlecasts for a similar, and in many cases in excess of the amount of design, balance, and QA effort as developing new Champions and Quests.  At that sort of volume, the ROI ended up not making sense to continue to develop these, so they were put on pause.[/p][p][b]What changed?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Battlerealm Brawl[/b] - This was a major inflection point for Relic sentiment in the community. When players saw how Battlecasts could clutch top-tier competitive fights, players became much more engaged with the system. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Battlegrounds[/b] - As players engaged more with the new Battlegrounds game mode, and started running multiple Battlegrounds Decks, it started to become a major pain point to move your Relics between Champions in each of your Decks and across other modes in-game. Players started proactively asking for more Relics.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Some Lessons Learned[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Strikers Good![/b] - Players really enjoyed the combo-extending functionality of the Strikers.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Complexity Bad![/b] - Our hypothesis that end-game players wanted more crunchy Champion customization options proved incorrect. Relic management was generally perceived as another maintenance chore, rather than an exciting new way to customize your Champions. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Overly Cautious[/b] - Relics had the potential to blow up the game’s balance, so we were very conservative with their rollout (initially limited to certain game modes, lower rarity versions weren’t that strong, and higher rarity Relics required significant time to obtain, etc.) In hindsight, though, being so conservative undercut their release and compounded the underwhelmed player reception. [/p][/*][/list][p][b]Introducing… STATCASTS! [/b][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd-bDSHzie7yeEvWHS6wM6Av7Y_e-9axoBfDK2dWP-MQvCGqjxcFOthMQ8V_TiPT5hXiD1SeYpiUl7Wq_j7ZE72EsFQYZBc5YSlU2rMo8xJsSKGoBjespfm8Gt063fAZiyRqcrC?key=XlYMFDjdAnNykOSVyBVMGA"][/img][/p][p]After a lot of internal iteration on how to address the above issues, and what a compelling new Relic type could look like (within the limitations of the existing system), we will be introducing Statcasts to the Contest come August and beyond!
At a high level, they’ll be composed of…[/p][list][*][p][b]Striker:[/b] Yes, Statcasts will STILL have the combo-extending Strikers you know and love[/p][/*][*][p][b]Primary Attribute:[/b] Each Statcast will have a Stat that it boosts by a large amount (e.g. Crit Damage, Special Damage, Block Proficiency, etc.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Secondary Attribute:[/b] Each Statcast will have a Stat that it boosts by a smaller amount (e.g. Crit Damage, Special Damage, Block Proficiency, etc.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Singular Runes:[/b] Each Rune will only have one option, no need to swap it around [/p][/*][*][p][b]Active on Defense:[/b] Statcast Rune effects will be active on DEFENSE (however, Defenders will [b]NOT[/b] be able to use Strikers) [/p][/*][*][p][b]UX Improvements:[/b] We will be introducing several menuflow improvements to make it easier to manage and understand your Relics (both Battlecasts & Statcasts post August )[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Each Statcast Relic statue will map to a specific combination of a Class and a Primary Attribute (e.g. Hulkling = Cosmic Armor Penetration), and each Statcast will have a number of Secondary Attribute variants (Armor Pen + Crit Rate, Armor Pen + Special Damage, Armor Pen + Energy Resist, etc.) This mix and match approach will allow us to produce lots of Statcasts and address the Relic scarcity issue that has caused Summoners so much frustration. [/p][p][/p][p][b]What does this mean for the future of Battlecasts?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Never say never. We won’t say that we’ll never make another Battlecast, but for right now, we don’t have any plans to make more.
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]What were some of the challenges in building out Statcast Relics?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Scale was the biggest challenge we faced. Relics were originally built to be bespoke, 1-off’s and hand crafted, both in terms of the UX (Screens and other Interactions) as well as on the back-end where we actually build the data which drives them. So it took some figuring out to find ways to adapt those bones to our new vision without just re-doing a huge feature, which took significant time and resources to build originally, with an intentionally smaller team and shorter timeline.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]
When can players expect to see Statcast Relics added to the contest?[/b][/p][list][*][p]The first batch will be released in our 52.0 build in August.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]
How can players get them?[/b][/p][list][*][p]We will run an initial Alliance Event with a mix of rarities, along with different crystal bundles for players to begin their collections.
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Can I use my existing relic crystal shards?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Since Battlecasts have lived in the ecosystem for so long, players have wildly varying amounts of relic shards hoarded, making it impossible for us to release Statcasts into the existing pool without creating a huge imbalance in access. [/p][/*][*][p]Because of this, Statcast Relics will be obtainable through a NEW form of Shards and will not be added to existing crystal pools.
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]What about my existing Relic resources???[/b][/p][list][*][p]Existing and future Alloys and Embers will work on both Battlecasts and Statcasts [/p][/*][*][p]Existing and future Relics Gems (Awakening, Innate, Rank Up) will work on both Battlecasts and Statcasts
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]7 Star Relics?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Statcasts will be available at 5-7 Star rarities. [/p][/*][*][p]Battlecasts will remain at the existing 3-6 Star rarities for now
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]How many Statcast Relics are we talkin’ about here?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Our initial batch, slated for 52.0 release, is a whopping 60 unique Statcast Relics Per Rarity! [/p][/*][*][p]As a reminder, each Statcast Relic will have a Primary Attribute and a Secondary Attribute. There will be 2 Primary Attribute Relics per class, resulting in 12 unique statues, and each of them will have 5 possible Secondaries, getting us to that total of 60. [/p][/*][*][p]AND… we have even MORE slated for subsequent builds, so there’s a lot to be ecSTATic about..[/p][/*][/list][p][b]
What are some min-maxing opportunities you can think of theoretically?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Most of the Attributes that the Statcast Relics can currently boost go through the diminishing returns curve, so many of the best combinations involve either buffing relatively lower stats or finding champions with strong interactions with specific stats. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]For example, increasing the Block Proficiency of Champions like Guillotine (Deathless or otherwise), Tigra, or Mr Negative can make them much more survivable, and increasing the low base Critical Rating of someone like Kingpin or Hulkbuster can have a large impact of their damage output. Further, Lady Deathstrike gets additional Damage from increasing her Armor Rating, and Champions like Jack O’Lantern, Shuri, and Guardian all scale damaging effects with their Critical Damage Rating. What theories do you have?[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Balance Update: Okoye and Gentle
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey all[/b],[/p][p]Balance Team here with an update on the latest round of Champions up for review, Okoye and Gentle![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Okoye[/b][/h2][p]Our fearless representative from the Dora Milaje in Okoye was designed as a high damage Attacker, leveraging frequent access to Bleed and Shock Debuffs as her primary damage source, with a few tools to counter defensive abilities commonly used by Science opponents. In a nutshell: Inflict lots of DOT’s + build lots of Combo! So far, we’re seeing her strong damage output and open Attacker loop shine across multiple game modes, proving to be a strong attacking option into a large gauntlet of tricky Defenders in Battlegrounds and Alliance War while also being an effective option in other Quests with longer encounters. As a result, no changes incoming for Okoye. [/p][p][/p][h2][b]Gentle[/b][/h2][p]Gentle, the Mutant from Wakanda, had a few hard-hitting Skill Champions in his sights, leveraging strong damage mitigation (Reinforce, Physical Resistance) to protect his health and the ability to create openings with Unstoppable to comfortably take down his opponents. So far, we like what we’re seeing with Gentle’s usage and matchup spread, proving to be a safe and reliable Alliance War Attacker against a group of traditionally tricky spots on the map. Gentle’s performance as a Defender is also in a healthy place, providing Battlegrounds decks with a speed bump to counter Attackers who rely on Physical Damage and Critical Hits as their primary damage source. notes.title: V51.0 Release Notes
notes.content:
The official V51.0 Release Notes for Marvel Contest of Champions are here!

[h1]New Champions[/h1]

[h2]Nico Minoru[/h2]

Nico Minoru was a relatively normal goth teenager until she and several of her childhood friends accidentally witnessed their parents performing a human sacrifice. With the help of the Staff of One, stolen from her own mother, Nico and the other Runaways managed to defeat their parents. They were then forced to quickly mature into full superheroes by the resulting power vacuum in Los Angeles.

[h2]Karolina Dean [/h2]

After leading a somewhat normal teenage life, Karolina Dean and her classmates discovered their parents were part of an evil organization that sacrificed teenagers to gods to create a utopia. After running away and eventually shutting down the organization, the group forged their own bizarre family, doing their best to move forward into the future, even if their past manages to keep up with them wherever they go. Despite the hiccups and constant teen drama, Karolina uses her Majesdanian powers to make the world a better place. As long as she has Nico, her friends, and the sun in the sky, Karolina always finds a way to shine bright!

[h1]Champion Updates [/h1]

[h2]Captain Britain Rework[/h2]

    A Fresh defensive threat in The Contest, with Neuroshock at the forefront of her kit.
    Tankier than ever, with Safeguard now in her kit, she’s going to need a lot more from the attackers to take her down.
    The ever present threat of Neuroshocks, and her Psionic mode being deadlier than ever, players are going to need to be very intentful with how they answer her.
    As an attacker, expect to ramp a ton of Prowess passives, and dish out massive DOT damage.

[h1]Fantastic FORCE Saga[/h1]

With so many dangers in The Battlerealm, the Fantastic Four have wisely decided to expand their ranks into The Fantastic FORCE. Each OG member of the Four is now a team captain recruiting Champions (and hopefully The Summoner) to assist them in defending The Battlerealm. Collect Research Grants throughout The Contest to trade in for up to a 7-Star Mister Fantastic!

[h1]Event Quest – At Any Price[/h1]

Members of the super-team The Runaways, Karolina Dean and Nico Minoru, have found themselves in The Contest of Champions. Far from home and low on options they have teamed up with both The Summoner and a dark bargain from Dormammu. Will this deal be a fair trade of power and promises? Or will the daring duo find themselves with more than they bargained for? Find out AT ANY PRICE!

[h1]Side Quest – Vaults Of Variance[/h1]

While researching new arrivals Nico and Karolina who managed to wander INTO The Contest, Reed Richards wanted to see if it was possible to recreate that mix of mystical and cosmic chaos to EXIT The Contest. While his findings were not conclusive, he did manage to open limited access to nearby pocket-dimensions which all contain vicious variants of the Fantastic Four themselves. These anomalies will require careful research and guarding. Luckily The Summoner is on the scene to gather samples and defeat foes.

To further protect his important science assistance, Reed Richards has activated some Fantastic Force Saga power for select Champions. This month many Champions may find themselves empowered with special abilities from the ever-lovin’ blue eyed Thing!

[h1]Wheel of Fate [/h1]

Within the twisting confines of The Battlerealm, another Quest has surfaced. The defenders will be familiar, but your options will become more limited between the different difficulties of the Quest.

Wheel of Fate is a new challenge Quest that utilizes an upgrade to our swap nodes. Not only will Summoners need to swap out their Champion after each fight, but the Champions they can swap to will be restricted by Champion tags. Test your roster depth and knowledge in Wheel of Fate!

[h1]Captain Britain Double Track Event[/h1]

Captain Britain has been reworked and is available for a limited time from the Platinum Track of a new Double Track Event! Complete challenges daily to unlock rewards and claim up to a 7-Star Reworked Captain Britain.

[h1]Solvarch Eidol Chase[/h1]

A new Eidol has entered The Contest! Keep an eye out around The Battlerealm for Shatter Essence and collect it during the Fantastic FORCE Saga to trade in for the brand new Eidol, Solvarch!

[h1]Pride Event [/h1]

Nico Minoru and Karolina Dean of The Runaways are on their way to The Contest! With their powerful looks and stunning style they are already Runway Ready, are you? Get fighting fit and fashion forward during our Pride Month Event!

[h1]Bug Fixes and Improvements[/h1]

notes.title: Dev Diary – Radiance
notes.content:
Greetings Summoners!

Last month, Kabam Crashed gave us an in depth introduction to our new competitive currency Radiance. Checkout the full breakdown below so that you are ready to go when you take on our competitive modes!

[h1]Radiance[/h1]

Hi everyone, Kabam Crashed here with another Dev Diary. I am excited to share the details of our plans for Radiance, our new competitive currency. As always, I look forward to continuing this conversation as we implement it across our game modes in the coming months.

[h2]Background[/h2]

As discussed in the Battlegrounds Dev Diary, we are introducing a new currency – Radiance – which will make up the majority of ranked rewards in our competitive modes. The goal of this currency is threefold:

[olist]
[*] To make Ranked Rewards in our competitive modes easier to update
[*] To allow End-Game Summoners to choose which modes they want to play while remaining competitive
[*] To allow for more accurate planning over the volume of rewards distributed to competitive Summoners
[/olist]

While the introduction of Radiance will result in changes to Ranked Rewards that decreases the sources for currencies like Trophy Tokens, Radiance does not completely replace any existing currencies, at least for the moment.

Glory, Loyalty and Trophy Tokens are more engagement-based currencies that will still have a place in the game (Trophy Tokens, for instance will still be available in the Victory Track). Just to properly set expectations, Radiance will only be available for those who compete at the top of the game, roughly the top 100,000 players in Battlegrounds, Alliance War, and Alliance Quest.

[h2]Game Modes[/h2]

Radiance will first be implemented in Battlegrounds. In the Battlegrounds Dev Diary, I said rewards updates in Alliance War and Alliance Quest will follow later this year. However, in order to do this properly we basically had to work out what the rewards in those modes would look like as we planned Battlegrounds, so we are actually very close to having tuning for those done as well. I’m now anticipating the updates to Alliance War and Alliance Quest by this Summer at the latest.

The updates will amount to enormous reward bumps in Battlegrounds and regular Alliance Quest. Because Alliance War and Alliance Quest Raids Ranked Rewards have been updated much more recently, those modes will see more modest value increases, though obviously there will be a lot more agency over the resources Summoners choose to spend this very valuable currency on.

I’m expecting the tuning of the Ranked Rewards and store will lead to some pretty significant FOMO for Summoners who aren’t competing in these modes. To this I will say, we know there is a gap in our competitive ecosystem right now. I see this as a 2X2 matrix of Alliance vs. Solo and PVP vs PVE vectors. Right now one of those quadrants is empty.

[h2]Marvel Contest of Champions Competitive Ecosystem[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45310472/14e5da85650c4285b771f194fbb219195b3a1b46.png[/img]

In my Dev Diary, I mentioned we are working on a new game mode, and that game mode will fill in this missing piece of the puzzle. Like Alliance Quest, it will focus on roster strength as the main driver for success, but it will be a solo ranked experience rather than one that forces you to rely on other Summoners. More details about this mode can be expected later this year.

In the meantime, stretch out those thumbs because I’m expecting our other three competitive modes to see a lot more interest in competitive play.

[h2]Radiance Store[/h2]

So with that out of the way let’s get into the details. The Radiance store will focus on Champion acquisition and Rank-Up materials, but will also feature consumables and other items. Champion acquisition and Rank-Up materials will reset every 35 days, alongside the Battlegrounds cycle. Consumables will reset every 7 days. 

There will also be limited purchase items which do not reset. Some of these, like a Mastery Point, and the Deathless Piece Selectors will be available indefinitely. Other items will only be available for one cycle. These single-cycle items will start to appear in the store later this year, after Radiance is added to Alliance War and Alliance Quest.

The Radiance store is going to be the premium store in Marvel Contest of Champions. A lot of lower tier items will not be available. However, should someone for some reason want to spend Radiance on lower tier Catalysts or Alloys, Summoners will be able to exchange Radiance for Trophy Tokens to access the Trophy Token store.

[h2]Store Access and Pricing[/h2]

Many of the decisions related to Radiance were done with ease of update in mind. For this reason, there is no differentiation in pricing for different Progressions. Any Summoner Thronebreaker and above will have access to the full store.

Cavalier and below Summoners will only have access to the Trophy Token trade-in. Another factor is, as I said earlier, only roughly the top 100,000 Summoners will have meaningful access to Radiance. Since there are more than 100,000 Valiant players, we anticipate almost all Radiance will be earned by the top Progression, meaning building out pricing for lower Progressions would have been a waste of resources.

A similar philosophy was applied to store pricing. There are some weird prices, and that’s because we have set up the store so that pricing is entirely formulaic. This means no hand-tuning of pricing, which means it will be much easier to update than our other stores.

[h2]Store Updates[/h2]

Because of the design decisions discussed above, this store will be much easier to update. Our goal is to do so regularly. I’m not going to give a definitive time frame, but I can say we would be targeting roughly 3 to 4 updates every year.

I do want to set some expectations here though. More frequent updates will often mean smaller updates. Don’t expect to see large swings in prices for most items, and many items won’t change in price at all from one update to the next.

[h2]Store Curves[/h2]

Some Summoners will earn 10,000 Radiance a cycle, some will earn 100,000 Radiance a cycle and some may earn close to 1,000,000 Radiance a cycle. The only way to tune it so the Summoner that earns 10,000 can get something meaningful while the Summoner that earns 1,000,000 doesn’t run out of stuff to buy is to apply a curve. However, unlike the curves in the Glory store, which are linear, the Radiance store has curves that are much flatter for the first few purchases with a faster acceleration later in the curve. This means more purchases at close to the base price before large cost increases.

[h2]Store Tuning[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45310472/e2bc7a8c12261428b974f83416f56e190e3fe4cc.png[/img]

notes.title: Dev Diary – Adrenaline
notes.content:
Greetings Summoners!

Here is another of our recent Dev Diaries, this time covering Adrenaline thanks to our recently reworked Cyclops (Blue Team). Take a look!

[h1]Adrenaline[/h1]

Adrenaline has existed in the Contest for over seven years now (after typing this I took a break to stare out the window for a few minutes because how has it possibly been that long). It was originally announced in the post below, and has mostly lived on quietly in the background, improving the survivability of 6 and 7-star champions and allowing Summoners to clutch out fights that otherwise wouldn’t have gone their way. With the rebuild of Cyclops (Blue Team), though, we’re breaking new ground in what exactly Adrenaline means in the Contest, so we’d like to offer a refresher.

[url=https://forums.playcontestofchampions.com/en/discussion/46362/adrenaline-what-is-it-and-how-does-it-work]Adrenaline: What is it, and How Does it Work?[/url]

As a quick reminder, usually Adrenaline is gained as a 6 or 7-star Attacker is struck by or Blocks an incoming hit. Damage is taken as normal, but a portion of that hit damage is stored in the Health Bar as a white subsection of the larger Bar. Only hit damage is stored, so “red numbers” such as Regeneration reversal or damaging effects do not factor in. “Maximum Adrenaline” is equal to your maximum Health (or effectively your maximum Health minus 1), and you cannot store more Adrenaline than you have room for in your Health Bar, meaning you cannot have more Adrenaline than your missing Health. Additionally, any Health recovered from Regeneration or similar abilities will be subtracted from your stored Adrenaline.

Adrenaline is then converted back into Health when you deal damage to the Opponent. The amount converted is not based on the damage dealt, but instead on what level of attack you are throwing (eg; Light, Heavy, Special 3) and on your Champion’s Base Attack Rating.

Neither the initial storage of Adrenaline nor the conversion back into Health are affected by Regeneration Rate or abilities that block Healing (as it is not technically healing). Additionally, because Adrenaline is not itself Health, it cannot prevent a knockout if your Health is reduced to 0, and it does not persist into the next fight if you have any left over when a fight ends.

All of the above rules are unchanged and still apply. But going forward, we also have some new toys mechanics that may find their way to Champions in the future.

For starters, you may see Champions that increase or decrease their Combat Adrenaline, which is the familiar method of storage via hit damage. Until now, this rate (when not 0) has always been 30%, or 35% for those 7-stars whose Summoners haven’t yet changed their Stat Focus selections, but now more is possible. Note that anything that increases Combat Adrenaline will be a flat increase, meaning that increasing a 6-star’s Combat Adrenaline by +20% will cause 50% of incoming hit damage to be stored, rather than 36%. For 1 through 5-star Champions, Combat Adrenaline is 0%, but this can be increased by other effects!

We can also now grant Adrenaline in other places, which will be referred to as Ability Adrenaline. As you may have picked up on, this is very similar to the split between Combat and Ability Power Rates. On the conversion side, you may also see Champions that convert more Adrenaline with certain attacks, or in lump sums on other triggers! Lastly, to help you better process all of this more easily, we’ve changed the display of Adrenaline conversion to show up as blue numbers, rather than green, so you can better distinguish this health gain from traditional Regeneration.

To look down the road a bit, if you’re starting to worry about us interfering with the Adrenaline you’re used to, let me assure you that is not the goal here. What we want here is to be able to start building more Champions that hook into this unique and powerful resource, and to let you interact with it in ways that feel familiar from other parts of the game. For now, Cyclops dips a toe into these new waters with a pretty simple interaction in his Signature Ability, but keep an eye out for future Champions that expand on these mechanics in bewitching new ways!

notes.title: Dev Diary – AI Deep Dive
notes.content:
[h1]Intro[/h1]

Greetings Summoners! As we get closer to our Steam launch we will be sharing some of our most recent Dev Diaries as well as updates to in-game events. As Marvel Contest of Champions is Cross Save and Cross Progression, changes made now will be reflected when we launch on Steam.

Back in April the Game Team took some time to provide greater insight into AI in our game, we hope you find this as interesting as helpful as others have!

[h1]AI Deep Dive[/h1]

AI is a hot topic in our community, and there are a lot of misconceptions around what it is and how it works, so we thought it would be a good time for us to pull back the curtain on how it functions, and talk about where it’s going in the future.

Before we begin, it’s important to separate what exactly the AI controls from how it makes its decisions, as those are two different conversations. We plan to have both conversations, but for this particular post, we want to focus on the latter. Then we’ll dedicate a future post to clarifying what things do and don’t fall under the umbrella of AI in the first place.

So to start with some important questions –

[h3]What is the AI?[/h3]

[list]
[*] Not an actual artificial intelligence
[*] A frame perfect button masher with random outputs ( More on this later )
[*] Too random, but also doesn’t respect randomness (It’s too random for designers to control, but also has old, hard rules that make it harder to understand than true randomness at times) making this very difficult to debug
[/list]

[h3]What Does the AI know?[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Actions [/b]– What “buttons” are available to press (Light, Medium, Heavy, Special Attacks, Block, etc.)
[*] [b]Distance [/b]– How far apart are the Attacker & Defender
[*] [b]State [/b]– What animation state are the characters in (Idle, Block, Dash, Special Attack, Hit Stun, etc.)
[/list]

[h3]What Doesn’t the AI know?[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Effects [/b]– The AI doesn’t know about the existence of Buffs, Debuffs, Passives, Timers, Nodes, Traps, etc. There are effects that modify how it makes its random decisions, but it doesn’t know if they’re active or not.
[*] [b]Masteries [/b]– The AI doesn’t know about the existence of Masteries, even ones that now live at the center of MCoC gameplay. As an example, the AI is never attempting to Parry, because it doesn’t know what that is or does. It simply tries to block incoming hits, and this can cause it to Parry. The same goes for Dexterity, no matter how impressive the performance.
[*] [b]Memory [/b]– The AI only knows about the present game state; it has no concept of things that happened earlier in the fight. This also means that it has no idea if it’s attempting an action for the first time in the fight or for the twentieth time in a row.
[/list]

[h3]How does the AI make decisions?[/h3]
[list]
[*] Each Action the AI can take is given a weighted chance of being rolled.
[*] Every frame the AI rolls to see what Action it attempts, even if it is already performing another one.
[*] There are some rules that make an Action invalid (e.g. you can’t do this Action if you’re in this state, you can’t do this Action if your distance to the opponent is too great, and so on.)
[*] If the AI rolls an invalid Action, it will keep re-rolling until it finds a valid one, as the animation below shows.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45310472/58809b090a374fb7030a5ddabff84d9a62488571.gif[/img]

You can see here each frame has an event chain based on what rolls and decisions are happening. Here’s a closer look at an example of what that chain could look like at any given moment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45310472/386c45856fadd72ddf0b8c29282f7b80d86ccfcf.png[/img]

Obviously, it’s impossible for all of these things to actually occur, even the successful roles, but this creates a lot of noise when one is trying to figure out exactly why a certain outcome occurred.

[h3]What about the things that modify AI behavior?[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]AI Profiles[/b] – Each fight has an AI profile assigned that determines its default weights for rolling each Action. We primarily use two… “easy” for early game content, and “hard” for everything else.
[*] [b]Champion Specific Tuning[/b] – In rare cases, if a Champion relies on a specific Action as a core part of their gameplay loop, we can add additional weighting to that Action for that character (e.g. Heavy Attack on Doctor Doom). We do mean rare here – there are far fewer of these cases than players usually suspect.
[*] [b]Aggression [/b]– During the fight, hitting the Defender builds up a hidden Aggression stat, which adds more weight to certain attack Actions. This decays over time if you stop hitting the Defender. Both the growth and decay of this system vary by profile.
[*] [b]Mistakes [/b]– Another hidden system is “Mistakes.” The AI has a chance in the roll to make a bad decision, with the original intent of giving the player an opening to capitalize on.
[*] [b]Effects [/b]– There are effects that modify AI behavior (e.g. Taunt, Intimidate, Infuriate). They do this by adding weight to the targeted Action, such as a Special Attack in the case of Taunt, or by modifying the overall aggression of the system.
[/list]

[h3]What does this all mean?[/h3]
With all the above being said, the AI doesn’t really know why it’s hitting the buttons it’s hitting, but when it makes a decision, it does so instantly and with perfect information (Frame Perfect Button Masher). So if there’s any window the AI can capitalize on, it will eventually find it. Think of how you sometimes tap a light randomly and find that you’ve just intercepted your opponent, and now imagine you have the perfect reaction timing to turn that into a full combo every single time, and to block if you don’t and see yourself being attacked in turn. That kind of in-the-moment randomness is what everything the AI does is built from. So while behavior patterns do emerge based on the probability spread of the different Action rolls, the most universal truth of the AI is that unpredictability. Now, some of that is the point in a skill-based fighting game, where an element of your skill is reacting to new information, but the current system is more random than that.

It’s important to reiterate that the AI has no concept of techniques like parrying or intercepting. That’s why it’s so difficult to address certain kinds of issues, like the AI light intercepting the player too often, because there isn’t a system specifically for that behavior in place, and so there’s nothing we can cleanly tune up or down. We can change global aggression values or tell the AI to use light attacks less often or to block more often, but all of those cause significant collateral damage to the overall play experience. At the end of the day, when the button masher at the heart of the system sees your character vulnerable in front of it and in range for a light attack, it is going to see that as the only valid action some real percentage of the time.

For these reasons, our long-standing policy was that we simply wouldn’t change the AI at all. Why risk making gameplay worse overall when you can’t even be confident the change will have the intended effect? As we’ve said before, we decided last year that this approach was untenable. Too many small changes were happening whether we wanted them to or not – we’d optimize the way fights are loaded, or clean up some background variables, or find and fix a seemingly unrelated code bug, or do something crazy like upgrade the entire game to play and function at 60 frames per second instead of 30… And something somewhere would change without us being able to roll it back or even meaningfully make a change in the opposite direction.

For a while, we tried making those targeted fixes anyway, being as careful as possible, knowing we couldn’t just watch the system decay in front of us. But even as careful as we were (putting fixes through rigorous QA, internal playtesting, CCP playtesting, etc.), we still sometimes discovered unintended knock-on bugs after we pushed a fix live. (Or in the case of the Medium Intercept fix, fixed one problem only to uncover another that had been hiding beneath it). And so, despite some clear wins (defender reparry, special baiting for larger characters), we know that this slow, piecemeal approach isn’t working either.

One bright spot in this part of the story is that this process has brought huge improvements to our internal toolsets. Some of you may remember that we announced a refactor to some internal logic shortly before the release of Necropolis, which was instrumental in helping us more quickly diagnose bugs and test fixes. That change allowed us to build out fight recording and scripting tools, which have already been a huge help in finding and fixing bugs both with the AI and with other parts of the Contest, and has done a lot to set the stage for what comes next. Speaking of…

[h3]The Moment You’ve Been Waiting For?[/h3]
We don’t usually share this sort of information this early, but we want to continue this train of transparency and show you how seriously we are taking this. Our dearest and faithful Summoners, we’re actively in development on building a [b]Brand New[/b] AI system.

[b]AI 2.0[/b], to be exact!

Our goal with this rebuild is to gain the ability to actually do things like “just tune Intercept down.” Or to build a feedback loop where the AI actually understands that it has been throwing heavies against the far wall for 20 seconds and should maybe try something else. But first, we still need to build out new systems for perception and memory, and then for making decisions, and get those decisions as close to parity with the current system as possible. After all, that weird, random button masher is a core part of the Contest as we know it, and we don’t plan to start things off with a wild departure from what you’re used to. We know we won’t perfectly replicate the current experience, but we intend to get very close, only with access to many more tools and levers for further improvements.

Additionally, we are building this system so that we have the ability to roll it out carefully and deliberately. We don’t plan to surprise you one day with an announcement that the whole Contest has swapped over, but instead plan to test this first in only specific quests or game modes.

Now, this is still a long way out, and there will certainly be a number of challenges in delivering this, but we are committed to improving the player experience here, and even further, to keeping you in the loop as we build out this massive new addition to The Contest.

Until then, Summoners, good luck traversing The Battlerealm!
